historical_growth.revenue_3yr_cagr_note: FY2023-FY2026 (781.2 -> 1,253.4); FY2021-FY2026 5yr (427.2 -> 1,253.4). Both are inflated by the Trader Interactive (Jun-2022, consolidated from FY2023) and Webmotors (FY2023) acquisitions. Organic constant-currency growth has run 12% in FY25 and FY26, ~9.5% reported AUD in FY26 on the continuing (ex-Tyres) base.
historical_growth.eps_note: 3yr from FY2023 is meaningless: FY2023 EPS 1.813 carries a ~A$500m non-cash gain on revaluing the existing 49% Webmotors stake at step-up to control. 5yr FY2021 (0.526) -> FY2026 (0.829) = 9.5%.
historical_growth.equity_note: Equity jumped FY2021 (940m, A$600m TI raise) and FY2023 (3.1bn, A$1.2bn TI/Webmotors raise) then drifted down FY2024-26 on FX reserve moves and a >90% payout; book value is dominated by acquisition goodwill and says nothing about earning power here.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2021 162.0, FY2023 209.6, FY2026 430.0. Same acquisition inflation as revenue; SBC is immaterial (0.4-0.6% of revenue) so owner and reported CAGRs are within 0.2pp of each other.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 guidance midpoint (12.5% cc) less ~2.5pp FX translation drag; not any historical CAGR, all of which carry the FY2023/24 consolidation step.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (-3.4%) diverges >30% from revenue (17.1%) and owner-FCF (26.5%) CAGRs: the acquisition step-ups and the near-100% dividend payout break the equity series. Ignored for growth selection.

scenario_narratives.base: CAR Group delivers roughly the midpoint of its FY27 guidance (revenue +11-14% cc, EBITDA +10-13% cc) net of the 2-3pp AUD translation drag it has absorbed each of the last two years. Australia grows high single digits on dealer depth products and Instant Offer, Trader Interactive double digits as the commercial/truck vertical carries RV softness, Webmotors and Encar double digits on premium products and Guarantee/Home Delivery. Growth fades to 3.5% over ten years; EBITDA margin drifts from 53.5% to 56% as Latin America scales; acquired-intangible amortisation runs off so D&A converges to a 10.5% capex ratio; tax plus Webmotors-minority leakage rises from 25% to 28%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rates fall in the US and Brazil, the RV/powersports cycle turns, and the AI lead-nurture and C2C payments products prove to be yield levers rather than cost lines. Revenue compounds 13% -> 4% over the decade with margins reaching 58%; the four-market network-effect portfolio earns the 'global classifieds compounder' multiple the stock carried at A$38.
scenario_narratives.bear: The sceptics on FY27 guidance are right: a strong AUD and a weak US discretionary market leave reported growth at 6% and fading, Australian listing-price growth stalls under Facebook Marketplace and AutoTrader pressure, and management keeps investing through the slowdown so margins compress to 51.5%. Net debt/EBITDA of 1.8x is serviceable but rising finance costs and D&A squeeze statutory NPAT well below the adjusted figure the market is anchored on.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the consolidated group's unlevered owner FCF - statutory EBITDA (not the company's adjusted figure, which strips recurring restructuring/M&A/FX costs), leases as an operating cost, SBC expensed with a flat share count, NCI charged as leakage in the flows, acquired-intangible amortisation NOT perpetuated as a tax shield - discounted at an AUD WACC of 9%. The debate is entirely about growth durability and margin trajectory in four markets with different cycles; the balance sheet and accounting are clean, so risk is carried in the scenario weights and never in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: FX translation: ~58% of revenue in USD, BRL, KRW and CLP; a 5% AUD move is ~3% of group revenue and EBITDA before any operating change
Guidance credibility: FY26 finished at the bottom of its range and FY27 asks for 11-14% cc revenue growth; the base case already haircuts this to 10% reported
US recreational verticals (RV, powersports, marine investment) are the most cyclical part of the group and Trader Interactive is 27% of revenue
Australian yield growth depends on continued dealer price rises and depth-product uptake against Facebook Marketplace and the AutoTrader/CarsGuide network
Terminal value is ~60% of EV; each 1pp of WACC moves the base value by roughly A$3-4/share (see sensitivity grid)
Webmotors minority (30%, Santander) is charged at ~5% of NOPAT; if Brazil outgrows the group the leakage rises beyond the 28% terminal tax+NCI rate assumed

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average 378,704,494 from the FY2026 EPS note (basic 378,364,226 + 12,180 options + 328,088 performance rights); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. FY25 repurchase was A$0.7m only (employee-share-plan on-market purchases), FY26 nil; the flat count is a modelling convention, not a funded buyback.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company's own definition, FY26 AR net-debt note: borrowings A$1,524.6m (current 27.3 + non-current 1,497.4) less cash A$325.6m and term deposits A$0.9m = A$1,198.1m. Lease liabilities (A$77.2m: 11.3 current + 65.8 non-current) are EXCLUDED because leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B).
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income A$20.6m (interest received A$27.0m) sits in INVESTING cash flows in CAR's statement, so it is not inside reported FCF (OCF - capex) and there is nothing to strip. The company is net debt A$1.2bn, so the section-1(b) net-cash rule does not apply either. Interest PAID (A$94.0m) is in financing, so OCF is unlevered - consistent with discounting at WACC and deducting net debt.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR cash flow statement, 'non-cash employee benefits - share-based payments' add-back A$5.765m; no cash taxes on equity awards disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every year). SBC is 0.4-0.6% of revenue in every year FY2016-FY2026 - an SBC-light ASX market.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built WACC: risk-free 4.3% (AGB 10y), ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.0 for a scaled online marketplace -> cost of equity ~9.8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (A$1.5bn syndicated facilities, FY26 interest paid A$94m / avg gross debt A$1.45bn = 6.5% incl. fees), ~4.0% after tax; market-value weights ~88% equity (A$8.95bn cap) / 12% debt (A$1.2bn net) -> 9.1%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality, FX and US-RV risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) - leases as operating cost. FY26 lease cash = principal A$13.1m (financing) + interest A$3.2m (note 16 interest charge) = A$16.3m = 1.30% of revenue, charged inside owner EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (A$77.2m) excluded from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation: A$185.4m - A$15.8m ROU = A$169.6m = 13.5% of FY26 revenue.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows: NCI (Webmotors 30% held by Santander Brasil, plus minor others) took A$18.7m of FY26 profit, ~5% of unlevered NOPAT. Folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax+leakage driver: 1-(1-0.21)(1-0.05) = 25%. NCI book value (A$72.3m) is NOT deducted in the bridge. Calibration: FY26 EBIT (statutory EBITDA 667.3 + SBC 5.8 - SBC 5.8 - lease 16.3 - D&A ex-ROU 169.6) = 477 x (1-0.25) = A$358m vs reported attributable NPAT A$313.7m + post-tax net finance cost ~A$45m = A$359m. Ties.
inputs.ebitda_basis: STATUTORY EBITDA (PBT 423.7 + net finance costs 58.2 + D&A 185.4 = 667.3, 53.2% margin) plus the SBC expense it already contains (5.8) -> 673.0 pre-SBC = 53.7% of revenue, the anchor for ebitda_margin_path. The company's 'proforma/adjusted EBITDA' of A$700m (55.9%) adds back A$27m of restructuring, M&A and FX costs that have recurred every year (FY25 A$25.7m) and are treated as real costs here.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: operating company / marketplace). Confirmed against the associates question: since FY2023 Trader Interactive (100%) and Webmotors (70%) are fully CONSOLIDATED subsidiaries, so the statutory P&L and cash flows already carry their revenue, EBITDA, capex and tax; the only look-through item is the 30% Webmotors minority, handled as leakage above. No equity-accounted associates of any size remain, so no sum-of-parts is needed. HISTORY: FY2023 (+53%) and FY2024 (+41%) revenue steps are the Trader Interactive and Webmotors consolidations, not organic growth; the base path is anchored to FY27 guidance (revenue +11-14% cc, adjusted EBITDA +10-13% cc, D&A +16-19%, net finance costs A$66-72m, ETR 20-21%) haircut for the ~2-3pp AUD translation drag management flagged and for FY26 finishing at the bottom of its own range. FY2019/FY2020 rows include discontinued ops as reported. PRICE: regular-session Yahoo print; stock is near its 52-week low (21.47) after trading to 38.68 within the year. Working capital: dealer subscriptions are billed monthly, deferred revenue is small; FY26 OCF (577.2) vs EBITDA less cash tax (578.8) implies ~zero working-capital cash, so wc_capture 0. Owner FCF FY26 = 435.8 reported - 5.8 SBC = 430.0 (pre-NCI; the component build's FY0-equivalent after unlevered tax and NCI leakage is ~A$390m, 31% of revenue).

bear.narrative: Guidance missed the way RBC fears: FY27 revenue +6% reported after a 4-5pp FX drag and a soft US recreational market, Australian yield growth capped by AutoTrader/Facebook Marketplace pricing pressure, Korean data-privacy rules and Brazilian rates blunt the international engines. Investment in marine, Dealer Direct and Nexgate continues without the revenue, so margin slips to 51.5% and stays; capex stays at 11% while D&A only slowly converges. Higher tax leakage as US losses expire sooner.

base.narrative: FY27 at the guidance midpoint less FX drag (10% reported), decelerating to 3.5% by FY36 as Australia matures and LatAm/Asia growth normalises. EBITDA margin dips in FY27 (guidance has EBITDA growing 1pp slower than revenue on marine and Korea investment) then recovers ~25bp/yr to 56% as Latin America reaches Australian-style margins. D&A runs above capex for years as acquired-intangible amortisation (A$82m FY26) winds down, converging to capex (10.5%) by year 10 so no tax shelter is capitalised in perpetuity. Tax+NCI leakage 25% -> 28% as US tax losses deplete (guided ETR 20-21% now) and the faster-growing Webmotors minority takes a rising share.

bull.narrative: Top of the FY27 guidance range with a neutral AUD; US RV/powersports demand recovers as rates fall, LatAm dealer expansion and finance commissions keep Webmotors at 20%+, AI lead-conversion tools and C2C payments lift Australian yield. Margins expand ~45bp/yr to 58% on operating leverage; capex settles at 10% of revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs three independent things to go right (US RV recovery, a neutral-or-weaker AUD, and LatAm margins converging on Australia) while the new CEO's Elevate 2028 plan is still unproven. Bear lifted to 20% because ~58% of revenue is offshore translation exposure, FY26 landed at the bottom of its own guidance range, and 1.8x leverage removes the buffer a net-cash marketplace would have. No going-concern or single-regulator risk, so no case for 25%+.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
